subject.title: improve(gateway): bound visible history page reads

question: Is returning a versioned opaque `nextCursor` while accepting numeric cursor input for only one upgrade window the intended durable HTTP history compatibility contract?
rationale: This changes an externally observable gateway response representation; the diff supplies compatibility handling, but the duration and support expectations for existing clients require owner intent.

options.title: Preserve opaque replay compatibility
options.body: Keep opaque cursors as the new response form, accept legacy numeric input through a clearly defined deprecation window, and add final-head proof for both forms.

options.title: Keep numeric response cursors
options.body: Use the new internal keyset reader while retaining numeric response cursors until a separately versioned gateway API transition is approved.

options.title: Pause the response-contract change
options.body: Land only after the storage owner defines a broader gateway cursor-versioning policy for external consumers.

recommendation.title: Preserve opaque replay compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep opaque cursors as the new response form, accept legacy numeric input through a clearly defined deprecation window, and add final-head proof for both forms.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged current-main projection and history implementation make this the strongest available routing candidate for the HTTP cursor contract.
